messages:
maria: Quick RFC follow-up — thinking about a "residency lease" model to reduce noisy evictions for long-running decode/streaming workloads. idea: allocations can expose a soft lease (ms) and a small async extension API. When memory pressure hits, evictor asks for extensions before force-evicting.

sam: Can you sketch the API? sounds promising for streaming but worried about bookkeeping perf.

maria: super short sketch:
```
lease = allocator.acquire_lease(ptr, duration_ms=2000)  // returns lease_id
ok = lease.extend(add_ms=1000)  // non-blocking, returns true if extended
lease.release()
```
Evictor: calls try_request_extension(lease_id, delta) and gets back asap: {granted|denied|defer_until_ts}. if denied, it enqueues for immediate reclamation.

judy: Impl questions: where do we store lease state? per-allocation header? separate slab map? both cost perf.

maria: yea tradeoff. per-alloc header is simplest but bloats small allocations. slab-map keeps compact metadata but needs fast lookup (hash or per-slab radix). My prototype kept a 64-bit lease word in the slab header and used epoch counters to avoid ABA.

priya: how does this interact with KV cache and prefix caching? often we want to keep KV for same request chain but release quickly after done. would leases create pin-like semantics?

maria: leases are soft pins: they don't prevent migration/compression options. Evictor gets a chance to coordinate: if extension requested, runtime can try cheap fallbacks first: compress, quantize, migrate to host-staging, or move to shared read-only cache. Only after exhaustion do we force-free.

leo: Important to define SLOs: extension latency budget, max total pinned bytes. otherwise a noisy set of long-lived leases could starve others.

sam: Right — need global accounting. Proposal: each tenant/process gets N lease-credits and a global lease-eviction watermark triggers backpressure (reject new leases). Credits are reclaimed on release or after lease TTL.

judy: What about fairness across request types? decode vs embedding vs internal jobs? Should leases be taggable so evictor can prefer ephemeral workloads?

maria: +1 taggable leases: `lease.tag = "decode" | "batch" | "prefetch"`. Evictor policy table picks eviction order by tag priority and current pressure.

priya: Telemetry: we need metrics to decide defaults. suggest: lease_acquired_total, lease_extension_attempts, extension_granted_ratio, extension_latency_p99, lease_force_evictions_total, per-tag histograms.

infra-bot: deploy pipeline note — we should gate by feature flag; rolling rollout to canary GPU pool only.

leo: Implementation detail — extension should be cheap: do not require stopping the owner thread. Use atomic compare-exchange on lease deadline. On denial, owner might be racing; define semantic that denied extension == may be evicted at deadline.

sam: Edge-case: checkpointing/model parallelism holds pointers across requests. How do we avoid dangling leases when owner crashes? TTL helps but we should also expose an admin evict-by-lease command.

maria: agree. TTL + a small finalizer callback registered by owner (optional). If owner dies, finalizer won't run; evictor reclaims post-TTL. Also expose `allocator.force_reclaim(lease_id)` for ops.

judy: Cost model-wise: storing deadline timestamps increases metadata; on 1B small allocations that's heavy. Maybe only enable leases for allocations above size threshold or for allocations created via `acquire_residency(ptr, opts)` opt-in API.

maria: that was the plan: opt-in API or automatic if allocation used by streaming decoder path (we mark them). Default lease TTL small (1–2s) and extensions are short (100–500ms) to avoid long pins.

priya: Testing: we should add fuzz scenarios that simulate high churn + long sequences to measure tail latency and reclaim rates. Also measure cost delta vs baseline.

leo: rollout plan:
- RFC -> prototype in runtime branch (maria)
- canary on small GPU pool behind feature flag (infra-bot)
- gather metrics for 2 weeks, tweak defaults

maria: Action items:
- I’ll push prototype with per-slab lease word and opt-in API (PR by EOD Friday)
- @sam & @judy: review perf/metadata tradeoffs
- @priya: define telemetry dashboards/alerts for extension_granted_ratio and lease_force_evictions_total
- infra-bot: add canary flag in deploy pipeline

sam: ack. also please add a small doc section about expected semantics for model teams.

judy: quick concern: compaction/defrag interactions — if we move blocks as part of compaction, lease ids must survive relocation (use forwarding map). add to TODO.

maria: noted. forwarding map or store lease in slab-level not per-addr. will include options in PR.

priya: thanks — this seems like a pragmatic middle ground between hard pins and blind evictions. excited to try. :thumbsup:

leo: 👍 schedule a 30m follow-up after the canary metrics are in.

maria: thanks all — filing RFC follow-up doc w/ sketches and benchmarks link in thread soon.
